summary: Test-only change for TM-07 (agent enrollment and compromise). test/selftest_agent_revocation.py runs the control app in-process and connects to /v1/tunnel with a real aiohttp WebSocket client that signs challenge nonce + name + public key with an Ed25519 key, exactly like the agent's hello. It approves a pending key through registry.approve_node, opens two tunnel streams from the router side (one waiting for the response head, one with head and a body chunk already delivered by the test agent), revokes through registry.revoke_node and checks that both raise ClientError with the reason 'revoked', the agent receives status revoked before the close, the dynamic node leaves state.NODES and the registry entry is revoked. The revoked key reconnecting gets status revoked and a close, and never appears in state.PENDING or state.NODES. A second test sends MAX_ENROLL_PER_IP new keys from one address (pending), then one more: it is told to wait with the refusal, closed with 1008 and not written to the registry; an already approved key still connects. CI runs the test in the router job. No router code, configuration or policy change.

findings.evidence: Revocation of active streams and the enrollment flood were covered by unit checks of enrollment_denial and an end-to-end check of routing/registry state only.
findings.resolution: Wire-level tests with fault-injection evidence; out-of-band fingerprint verification and plausibility of a compromised approved agent's reports remain, so TM-07 stays open.

tests.command: Fault injection: revoke_node without tun.close_all('revoked') (registry.py, reverted)
tests.evidence: FAIL: 'revoked' not found in 'tunnel synthetic-gpu: tunnel closed'.

tests.command: Fault injection: handle_tunnel_v2 without the revoked-state refusal (registry.py, reverted)

limitations: Ran on Windows locally; Linux runs in CI.
Fingerprint verification before approval is an operator procedure and not testable here.
